story-and-authority.text: As a registry user, I can submit an authenticated request, find it despite pollution at the request address, and use a lawful exit with the ruled payments. As a reviewer, I can distinguish a reviewed component from a completed lifecycle and see every failed or uncovered obligation.

The acceptance items below were re-read from issue 529 on 18 October 2026. The constitution and the ruled Lean model are the behavioral authority. Singular's root model remains frozen at 4254a3073fe0457946eba0a68d974c999c930ebf, with Lean 4.27.0. The open-datum consumer amendment is the second chunk and is model-first: it is written, audited and recorded before any consumer is built on it. No root Lean or simulator-law change is authorized by this plan.

five-chunks-each-reviewed-and-pushed.text: Five chunks, each reviewed and pushed.

The owner's 18 October order replaces the earlier slice order, and moves the open-datum consumer model ahead of the economic fold. Each chunk has its own short story, acceptance mapping, exact fence, gate and audit checkpoints. Each reviewed chunk is pushed to the same branch, integration/498-protected-rejection, except that the model of chunk 2 travels with chunk 3 as set out after the table. Paths below are the expected areas of work; a later chunk's intake census fixes its exact file list before its first code commit.

Receipt-derived conformance rows, exact model/artifact bindings and the command-recovery obligations of the affected commands travel with their behavior's chunk. Publish uncovered rows; do not type a passing state or promote harness evidence to product acceptance. The adversarial items from issue529 require an actual mint refusal or demonstrated exit, not a blanket claim from a successful build.

If hosted checks for chunk 1 are red, their repair is the first item of the next push to the pull request (chunk 3, the next chunk that changes product code), with the problem and evidence recorded in that chunk's plan. It does not retroactively turn the failed check into a pass or hold the reviewed chunk 1 push.

order-the-model-and-the-pushes.text: Order, the model and the pushes.

The model comes first. The reviewed model of chunk 2, at an exact revision, is what the producers, bindings and fold of chunk 3 are written against. No consumer is accepted against a model that has not passed its own audit, and each push states the model revision it was built against.

One writer at a time. The model writer and the implementation writer never edit at the same time: the implementation writer stays at a committed boundary while the model is written, or finishes first.

The model is its own checkpoint. It is signed, audited on its own, and then pushed once to a backup branch on the remote, preserve/529-open-datum-model, so it does not live only on one disk; that branch triggers no workflow. The model reaches the integration branch only together with chunk 3's consumer migration, and the backup branch is deleted after that push.

Chunk 3 pushes once, green. It is cut into reviewed checkpoints (producers, conformance bindings, fold). No checkpoint is pushed with a conformance row knowingly red, and no legacy behavior is repinned to the new law.

The bindings follow the model's output. The statement header digests in Controls.hs are set from the amended model's own output, and replace the old ones only where the product evidence then shows the new law; no check is disabled to make that happen.
Every implementation push has its affected journeys green. Chunks 3 and 4 each name the journeys their changes can affect, and the push is accepted only when those journeys are green.

shared-ownership-and-intake.text: Issue495 owns the mismatch proof against the authenticated referenced root, remaining per-member batch rejection admission not covered here, and state-validator work beyond the minimum cut above. Issue529 owns the shared reference-state helper and expiry ground. A legacy fold is not an economic fold merely because it has been renamed.

Before a chunk's first code commit, perform one census of every validator/hash consumer: counts, title lists, source pins, goldens, identity manifests, declared-change records and journeys. Put every relevant hit in that chunk's fence at the start. A later-discovered mechanical consumer is an intake miss to repair within the chunk, not a new scope question. A semantic change, model conflict or change beyond the mechanical consequence remains a question. No expected result is weakened to make a check green.

The approved Sonnet commit owner writes implementation and the persistent Sol auditor independently inspects checkpoints without product execution. No extra implementation seats are authorized. For chunk 2, the already-approved Codex gpt-6-astra high Lean writer works between Sonnet slices, one writer at a time, using the same persistent auditor. The custody decision formerly held as Q003 is settled by the operator's 17 October treasury ruling; its model amendment still precedes code acceptance.

verification-and-delivery.text: Every build, test and packaged control uses its exact command inside this wrapper:

There is no aggregate execution budget. A single cap hit is recorded and follows its explicit ruling or becomes a question. Use the narrowest real changed-behavior checks; preserve RED-before-GREEN evidence and distinguish setup failure, refusal, acceptance, local receipts and hosted execution. Record the candidate/tree, command, exit, duration and evidence hash. Do not replay hosted job lists locally.

For chunk1, finish the in-flight comparison fixup and review-record corrections, obtain review012 approval, rebase once, inspect status and the log, run just ci once, then push and open the draft PR. Neither Demo1 nor the later economic fold holds this first push. The failed local archive attempt and the unexecuted deployment carrier remain explicit; hosted CI supplies their evidence. Later chunks repeat their own plan, audit and push cycle.

Only signed commits, with no attribution trailers, enter the pushed range. Use the repository PR template with model revision, implementation mapping and verification limits. The first draft title is Protected rejection (1.0.0). Keep it draft and held for the 22 October review; this owner never merges. No child PRs or GitHub comments; inspect CI through gh run list and gh run view, not gh pr checks.
